speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Please tell me, how long have you been experiencing fever, skin lesions, and wrist pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Lyme disease (erythema migrans or early disseminated stage) with reactive arthritis.

The patient's history of a self-resolving knee pain, recent camping trip in Minnesota, and current wrist pain with chills suggests Lyme carditis or Lyme arthritis. I would like to request the following tests: Lyme serology (ELISA and Western Blot), Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR), and C-Reactive Protein (CRP). Additionally, please provide images of the wrist and any skin lesions.
